newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says no problem with Belo Nobel remarks.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says no problem with Belo Nobel remarks.

text.p: Indonesia said on Tuesday it had "no problem with" reported remarks by East Timorese Nobel Peace Prize winner Bishop Carlos Belo, who was only asking for reconciliation and an end to violence in the territory.
The Roman Catholic bishop cleric and self-exiled activist Jose Ramos Horta received their gold medals and diplomas on Tuesday at a ceremony in Norway.

Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas, commenting on reported remarks by Belos, told a news conference: "From what I hear he was only asking for peace in East Timor, for reconciliation and end for violence."
"He was not talking about any political solution and that is precisely the role he has been playing and ought to be playing."
He added: "That's fine. That is what a shepherd of a flock, the head of the Catholic church should do, so we have no problem with his statements."
Belo, 48, said in his acceptance speech that the people of East Timor wanted peace and respect for human rights.

"It is high time that the guns of war are silenced in East Timor, once and forever. It is high time that tranquillity is returned to the lives of the people of my homeland. It is high time that there be authentic dialogue," he said in Oslo.
Alatas declined to comment on advance copies of the address.
"Dialogue with whom and between whom?" Alatas asked reporters. "If it is with Ramos Horta, there is the AETD (the U.N.-sponsored All-inclusive East Timorese Dialogue)," he said.
"The problem (of East Timor) must be solved by Indonesia and Portugal and it cannot be solved by other groups," he said.

Indonesia invaded East Timor in December 1975 and declared the territory its 27th province the following July in a move not recognised by the United Nations which regards Portugal as the administering power.

In October, Belo was attacked by senior members of the Indonesian government for reported remarks in a German magazine that the Indonesian military treated East Timorese as "scabby dogs" and "slaves".
Last month Belo denied he had used the word "scabby".
